cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, and friend, it's short but it is LOADED. David tells us what the LORD said to someone David calls my Lord. Lean in, because this is one conversation you do NOT want to miss.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to the one David calls my Lord. What does the LORD tell Him to do?

answers.text: Go out ahead of My army

cards.question: The LORD tells David's Lord to sit at the LORD's right hand until the enemies of David's Lord come and make peace with Him.

cards.text: His enemies, made a footstool for His feet. And friend, I know footstool life, because in that junk drawer takeout menus sat on ME for YEARS.

Centuries later, Jesus asks the Pharisees, the religious leaders, whose son the Christ is, and they say David's. So Jesus points them right to this line and asks how David can call Him Lord (Matthew 22:41-45).

cards.question: Next, the LORD extends the mighty scepter of David's Lord. Where does it reach out from?
The LORD extends the mighty scepter of David's Lord from Zion and tells Him to wait until every enemy is gone before He starts to rule.

cards.text: Not after the enemies are gone, but right there “in the midst of Your enemies.” Then David turns to His people on His day of battle.

cards.question: On the day of battle for David's Lord, His people have to be dragged into the fight.

cards.text: WILLING, friend, and that is HUGE, because you ask the group chat who can help move a couch and suddenly everybody's phone is dead. Then David paints it in big pictures: holy splendor, the womb of the dawn, the dew of Your youth.
Now the LORD makes an oath, and He will not change His mind. Me? I change my mind about toppings forty times a batch, so that line right there is humbling.

cards.question: The LORD swears an oath to David's Lord. What does He swear this Lord will be?
The LORD swore this and will not change His mind. What does that tell you about this promise?

answers.text: It lasts until the next king

cards.question: This priesthood is in the order of Melchizedek. In Genesis 14 he meets Abram after a battle, and he's king of Salem and ___ of God Most High.

cards.text: And the book of Hebrews connects it for us: Jesus has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 6:20).
Next, David says the Lord is at Your right hand. And a day of wrath is coming.

cards.question: David says the Lord is at Your right hand. In the day of His wrath, He will crush ___.
In this day of wrath, His judgment stays inside Israel's borders.

cards.text: He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead, and crush the leaders far and wide. Then the psalm ends on a quiet picture: He drinks from the brook by the road.

cards.question: In the psalm's last line, He drinks from the brook by the road, and therefore He lifts up His head. What picture does that leave you with?

findings.problem: The earlier cards told the baker the LORD's Lord sits at His right hand 'until' His enemies are made a footstool. A thoughtful baker reasoning from that would pick True for 'wait until every enemy is gone before He starts to rule.' The right answer, False, comes from 'Rule in the midst of Your enemies' (Ps 110:2), which no card has told yet. The earlier cards point the baker toward the wrong pick, so getting it right is luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Card 11 already says the LORD 'will not change His mind,' and the question repeats it. The right answer 'It is settled for good' only restates that line, so the answer is given away before it's asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'The LORD swore this,' which points back to the oath on card 12. That card isn't on screen, so the baker doesn't know what 'this' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'This priesthood,' which points back to card 12. The question never says whose priesthood it is or that the LORD swore it to David's Lord.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'In this day of wrath, His judgment...' points back to cards 16 and 17. The question doesn't say whose judgment it is or which day of wrath it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'He drinks from the brook by the road' without saying who 'He' is. The setup on card 19 isn't on screen anymore.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: All three answers call the one in verse 7 'A King,' but Psalm 110 never uses that title for Him. It calls Him 'my Lord' and 'the Lord,' and it only calls the ones He crushes kings. The text also leaves open who 'He' is in verses 5 to 7.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Three cards are spent outside Psalm 110. Card 5 is a story card on Matthew 22:41-45, card 15 is a story card on Hebrews 6:20, and card 14 is a choice card that tests Genesis 14:18. The docs allow outside facts 'when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter,' and they also say 'Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.' Neither rule says whether a whole card can go to a cross-reference, or whether a choice card can test a verse outside the passage.
findings.question: Can a story card be given entirely to a cross-reference outside the passage, like Jesus quoting Psalm 110 in Matthew 22 or Hebrews 6:20? Can a choice card test a verse outside the passage, like Genesis 14:18? Or should outside facts only ride along briefly on cards that tell the passage itself?
